criteria.text: Thyroid Eye Disease with a confirmed diagnosis of Graves’ disease (approval criterion 3).
Patient is 18 years of age or older (approval criterion 1).
Prescribed by or in consultation with ophthalmology, endocrinology, oculoplastic surgery or neuro-ophthalmology (approval criterion 2).
Documented euthyroid status or mild hypo-/hyperthyroidism with FT4 and FT3 levels <50% above or below normal limits (approval criterion 4).
Documented Clinical Activity Score at least 4 in the more severely affected eye(s) (approval criterion 5).
Active phase TED is non-sight threatening but significantly impacts daily living (approval criterion 6).
Documented inadequate response to high-dose glucocorticoids for at least one month, or contraindication or intolerance (approval criterion 7).
For females of reproductive potential: not pregnant and appropriate contraception before, during and 6 months after the last infusion (approval criterion 8).
Patient does not have poorly or uncontrolled diabetes (denial criterion 2).

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Tepezza (teprotumumab-trbw), an IGF-1R inhibitor. Version 1; Original 09/26/2022; Approval 11/18/22; Effective 1/2/2023.

Encoded: approval criteria 1–8 and denial criterion 2. The closed thyroid_eye_disease indication explicitly attests to Graves’ disease with TED (approval criterion 3). Denial criterion 1 is failure to meet approval criteria.
Thyroid status attestation requires FT4 AND FT3 levels <50% above or below normal limits for mild hypo-/hyperthyroidism; the option name is shorthand, not an inclusive 50% boundary.

Active TED impact examples: lid retraction ≥2 mm, moderate or severe soft tissue involvement, exophthalmos ≥3 mm above normal for race and gender, and/or inconstant or constant diplopia. These are examples within one attestation, not separate mandatory predicates.
Duration (notes only): initial approval 6 months; reauthorization not approved. Treatment is 8 infusions total given every 3 weeks.
Quantity/dosing (notes only): 10 mg/kg for the first infusion, followed by 20 mg/kg every 3 weeks for 7 additional infusions. HCPCS J3490. max_units is null; dosing and quantity are not evaluated.

Cautions (notes only): if an infusion reaction occurs, interrupt or slow infusion and use appropriate medical management. Monitor preexisting IBD for flare; discontinue if IBD worsens. Monitor glucose in all patients and treat hyperglycemia with glycemic control medications.
Documentation verification, duration, no reauthorization, infusion count, dosing, quantity and cautions require manual review; this pack remains partial. No PDL hit; pdl_status remains unknown.
